chunks.text: Account opening and know your customer (KYC)
headingPath: Account opening and know your customer (KYC)

chunks.text: This guide covers the steps a branch officer follows to open a personal current or savings account, the documents required, and the checks that protect the customer and the bank. It applies to walk-in customers at any branch. Business accounts follow a separate procedure.

Ask what the customer wants the account for: salary, savings, remittances or daily payments. The answer decides the product. A salaried customer who wants a debit card and mobile banking usually needs a current account. A customer saving for a goal needs a savings account, which pays profit monthly and has a minimum balance of five thousand rupees.

Explain the fees before the form: the debit card fee, the SMS alert fee and any minimum balance charge. A customer who learns about fees from the first statement will not trust the branch again.

Ask for the original computerized national identity card (CNIC). A photocopy, a photo on a phone or an expired card is not accepted. Check three things: the photograph matches the person, the card has not expired, and the name matches the form exactly, including spelling.

Run the NADRA verification in the system. The verification returns a match within seconds; if it fails twice, stop and involve the branch operations manager. Do not proceed on a third attempt without approval.

For customers who cannot sign, record a thumb impression in the presence of the branch operations manager and note it on the form.

The KYC form records the source of income, the expected monthly turnover, the purpose of the account and whether the customer is a politically exposed person. Fill it with the customer, not for the customer. Read each answer back.

Typical turnover for a salaried customer equals about one to two months of salary. A declared turnover that is ten times the salary needs an explanation and the manager's sign-off. Record the explanation in the notes field, not on a sticky note.

| Customer type | Documents |
| ------------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Salaried | CNIC, salary slip or employer letter |
| Self-employed | CNIC, proof of business such as a tax registration or a utility bill in the business name |
| Student | CNIC, student card, and the guardian's CNIC for customers under eighteen |
| Pensioner | CNIC and the pension book or letter |
| Overseas Pakistani | CNIC or NICOP and proof of overseas income |

Scan each document into the system, return the originals, and confirm on the checklist that every scan is readable.

Take the specimen signature on the card and in the system. The customer signs the same way every time; if the two signatures differ, ask for a third and keep the closest two. Capture the biometric thumb impression when the device is available.

Once the account is approved, give the customer the account number in writing, explain how to register for mobile banking, and tell them when the debit card will arrive (usually seven working days by courier to the registered address). Send the welcome SMS from the system.

Confirm the registered mobile number by reading back only the last four digits. The customer must own the number; a family member's number is not accepted because one-time passwords go to it.

- The customer's CNIC address differs from the current address. Accept a utility bill or a rental agreement as proof of the current address and record both.
- The customer wants to open the account for someone else. Every personal account is opened by the account holder in person. Explain politely and offer to book a time.
- The customer refuses to declare the source of income. The account cannot be opened. Explain that the declaration is a regulatory requirement, not a bank preference.
- The system verification is down. Do not open the account on paper. Take the customer's details, give a reference number and call back within one working day.

A complete opening takes about twenty minutes when the customer has every document. Tell the customer this at the start. Missing documents add a second visit; offer a checklist on the spot so the second visit succeeds.

Why do we verify identity before completing the KYC form? Because every later step depends on knowing who the customer is; a form completed for the wrong person cannot be corrected.

A customer declares a turnover of two million rupees a month on a salary of eighty thousand. What do you do? Ask for the reason, record it, and get the manager's sign-off before opening the account.

journey.title: Opening the Right Way: A Branch Officer's KYC Journey

story.premise: Ahmed, a newly hired branch officer, is guided by his senior colleague Sana through his first days of opening personal accounts, meeting a variety of customers whose situations test his understanding of KYC, documentation, and judgment calls.
story.setting: A busy urban branch of a fictional bank in Pakistan, on the officer's first week handling walk-in customers.

characters.role: Senior branch operations officer and mentor

characters.name: Mr. Iqbal
characters.role: Elderly pensioner customer opening a savings account

characters.name: Zara
characters.role: Young salaried customer wanting a current account and debit card

outline.title: Opening the Right Way: A Branch Officer's KYC Journey
outline.summary: A story-driven learning journey that walks a new branch officer through the full personal account opening process at a fictional bank branch, covering identity verification, KYC data capture, product matching, documentation, signatures, closing steps, and handling exceptions safely.

chapters.title: Meeting the Customer
chapters.arcBeat: The new officer greets the first walk-in customer and learns to ask the right questions before touching any form.

missions.title: What Does the Customer Really Need?
missions.objective: Determine the right account product based on customer intent and explain fees clearly.

missions.title: The Original CNIC Only
missions.objective: Correctly verify a customer's identity using CNIC checks and NADRA verification, including handling a failed match.

chapters.title: Building the File
chapters.arcBeat: The officer now assembles the full customer file, balancing accuracy with the pressure of a busy branch queue.

missions.title: Filling the KYC Form Together
missions.objective: Complete the KYC form with the customer, reading back answers and spotting a turnover mismatch that needs escalation.

missions.title: Matching Documents and Capturing Signatures
missions.objective: Select the correct required documents for different customer types and capture a valid specimen signature and biometric.

chapters.title: Sending the Customer Off Right
chapters.arcBeat: With the file complete, the officer must close the interaction properly so the customer trusts the branch from day one.

missions.title: The Welcome Message
missions.objective: Deliver the account number, explain mobile banking and card delivery, and confirm the customer's own mobile number.

chapters.title: When Things Don't Go as Planned
chapters.arcBeat: The officer faces the tricky cases that separate a well-trained staff member from one who guesses under pressure.

missions.title: Four Tricky Customers
missions.objective: Choose the correct response for mismatched address, third-party account requests, refused income declaration, and system downtime.

missions.title: A Full Account Opening, Start to Finish
missions.objective: Handle a complete walk-in customer case end to end, applying identity verification, KYC, documentation, signatures, and exception judgment.

concepts.name: Understanding customer needs and product fit
concepts.nameUr: کسٹمر کی ضرورت اور پروڈکٹ کا تعین
concepts.summary: Asking the customer the purpose of the account (salary, savings, remittances, payments) to decide between current and savings account, and explaining fees upfront before filling the form.

concepts.name: Verifying customer identity with CNIC and NADRA
concepts.nameUr: شناختی کارڈ اور نادرا سے تصدیق
concepts.summary: Checking the original CNIC for photo match, expiry and exact name match, running NADRA verification, and handling failed attempts or thumb impressions for customers who cannot sign.

concepts.name: Completing the KYC form accurately
concepts.nameUr: کے وائی سی فارم کی درست تکمیل
concepts.summary: Filling the KYC form together with the customer to record source of income, expected turnover, purpose of account and politically exposed person status, reading back each answer, and escalating unusual turnover declarations.

concepts.name: Capturing specimen signature and biometrics
concepts.summary: Taking a consistent specimen signature on the card and in the system, resolving mismatched signatures, and capturing a biometric thumb impression when available.

concepts.name: Closing the account opening interaction
concepts.nameUr: اکاؤنٹ کھولنے کے عمل کی تکمیل
concepts.summary: Giving the account number in writing, explaining mobile banking registration and debit card delivery timing, sending the welcome SMS, and confirming the registered mobile number belongs to the customer.

concepts.name: Handling exceptions and edge cases
concepts.summary: Responding correctly when the CNIC address differs from current address, someone tries to open an account for another person, a customer refuses to declare income source, or system verification is down.

concepts.name: Setting time expectations and reducing repeat visits
concepts.nameUr: وقت کی توقعات اور دوبارہ آمد کم کرنا
concepts.summary: Telling the customer the process takes about twenty minutes with complete documents, and offering a checklist to prevent a wasted second visit when documents are missing.

Which account will help me save, and what will it cost me?
I've been told other banks hide fees. Will you be upfront with me?

Staff mentions the minimum balance and monthly profit detail clearly.
Staff explains applicable fees before she signs any form.
Staff notes that explaining fees early avoids surprises and builds trust.

glossary.definition: Regulatory process to verify customer identity and record source of income before opening an account.
Computerized National Identity Card required as primary identity document for account opening.
System verification that confirms customer identity matches national database within seconds.
Account product for salaried customers needing debit card and mobile banking facilities.
Account product paying monthly profit with minimum balance of five thousand rupees.
Card issued to account holder for direct withdrawal and payment transactions.
Service allowing customers to access account and conduct transactions via mobile phone.
Lowest account balance required to maintain savings account without penalty charges.
Charge levied for sending short message service notifications to customer mobile.
Customer's authorized signature recorded on card and system for verification purposes.
Digital fingerprint capture of customer's thumb for identity verification when device available.
Unique identifier assigned to customer account after approval.
Temporary security code sent to registered mobile for transaction verification.
Customer's verified phone number linked to account for alerts and authentication.
Expected monthly transaction volume or income declared by customer in KYC form.
Individual holding significant public office requiring enhanced due diligence checks.
Declaration of how customer earns money, recorded in KYC form.
National Identity Card for Overseas Pakistanis accepted as identity document alternative.
Proof of current address accepted when CNIC address differs from residence.
Senior staff member who approves exceptions and supervises account opening procedures.
